docs.text: HardFOC driver AS5047U Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the ams OSRAM AS5047U 14-bit magnetic rotary position sensor. It reads angle, velocity and field diagnostics over CRC-protected SPI, configures the ABI, UVW and PWM outputs and programs the OTP, on any MCU with an SPI master. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a class with one method that moves a frame over SPI; it does the rest: frame building, CRC-8, the one-frame-late read protocol, read-back checks of every write, error flags and unit conversion. 14-bit on-axis magnetic rotary position sensor AS5047U ams OSRAM Measures Absolute angle, 14 bit (16384 positions per turn), velocity 24.141 °/s per LSB, AGC and field magnitude Host interface SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1) up to 10 MHz; 16-bit frames, or 24- and 32-bit frames with CRC-8 Outputs ABI incremental up to 4096 pulses per turn, UVW commutation for 1 to 7 pole pairs, 12-bit PWM Supply 4.5 V to 5.5 V on VDD (internal LDO), or 3.0 V to 3.6 V on VDD and VDD3V3 tied Limits Up to 28000 rpm, −40 °C to 150 °C, field 35 mT to 70 mT at the die Package and memory TSSOP-14; settings and zero position in volatile registers, burnable once to OTP Datasheet What you get ¶ One object per sensor. AS5047U<YourSpi> reads the angle ( GetAngle() , GetAngleDegrees() ), the uncompensated angle, velocity in LSB, °/s, rad/s or rpm, AGC and magnitude. See API guide . All three frame formats. 16-bit frames for the fastest reads, 24-bit frames with CRC, 32-bit frames with a PAD byte for daisy chains. Writes always use a CRC frame. See SPI protocol . Checked writes and replies. Every register write is read back on the next frame, every 24- and 32-bit reply the driver uses is CRC-checked, and port bus errors fail the call; all are retried on request. See API guide . The outputs configured in one call. ABI resolution, index width, UVW pole pairs, PWM pin, hysteresis, direction, zero position, DAEC and the adaptive filter. See Configuration . Typed registers. Every register is a struct with named bit fields, for ReadReg<>() and WriteReg() . OTP programming. The datasheet's burn sequence in ProgramOTP() . See OTP programming . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the chip's SPI slave. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the sensor, write the port, read an angle in about 15 lines. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: create it, read angle and velocity, check the field, configure, set up the outputs, use any register and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Encoder standing for as5047u::AS5047U<MySpi> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One AS5047U<SpiType> object per sensor. It offers three levels of access: Level Example Use it for Measurements GetAngleDegrees() , GetVelocityRPM() , GetAGC() Reading the sensor in a loop Setters SetZeroPosition() , SetABIResolution() , ConfigureInterface() One setting each, read-modify-write, verified Typed registers ReadReg<AS5047U_REG::SETTINGS2>() , WriteReg(s2) Any field a setter does not cover Group Members Angle GetAngle() , GetAngle(AngleUnit) , GetAngleDegrees() , GetAngleRadians() , GetRawAngle() Velocity GetVelocity() , GetVelocity(VelocityUnit) , GetVelocityDegPerSec() , GetVelocityRadPerSec() , GetVelocityRPM() Field and status GetAGC() , GetMagnitude() , GetDiagnostics() , GetErrorFlags() , GetStickyErrorFlags() , ClearStickyErrorFlags() , DumpStatus() Angle settings SetZeroPosition() , GetZeroPosition() , SetDirection() , SetDynamicAngleCompensation() , SetAngleOutputSource() Filter SetFilterPreset() , SetAdaptiveFilter() , SetFilterParameters() , GetFilterParameters() , GetAdaptiveFilterEnabled() Outputs ConfigureInterface() , SetABIResolution() , SetIndexPulseLength() , SetUVWPolePairs() , SetHysteresis() Chip Set150CTemperatureMode() , ProgramOTP() , VerifyOTP() Bus SetFrameFormat() , SetPad() , ComputeCRC8() Setters return bool : false means the value did not read back as written, or a frame failed on the bus (the port's transfer() returned false ). Measurements return the value (0 when the read failed); their errors are reported through the error flags (below). ReadReg(reg) reads any register and returns whether the read worked. Nothing throws and nothing allocates. Every call that takes a retries argument (default AS5047U_CFG::CRC_RETRIES , 0) repeats the access that many times when the chip reports a CRC or framing error. Create the driver ¶ // SPI_16 (no CRC), SPI_24 (CRC) or SPI_32 (CRC and a PAD byte) Encoder encoder ( spi , FrameFormat :: SPI_24 ); encoder . SetFrameFormat ( FrameFormat :: SPI_16 ); // later, e.g. for the fastest reads The constructor stores the port reference and the frame format; it sends nothing. Use SPI_24 unless you need the highest read rate ( SPI_16 ) or share the bus in a daisy chain ( SPI_32 with SetPad() ). SPI protocol explains the formats. Read angle and velocity ¶ const uint16_t lsb = encoder . GetAngle (); // ANGLECOM, 0..16383 (14 bit) const float deg = encoder . GetAngleDegrees (); // [0, 360) const float rad = encoder . GetAngle ( as5047u :: AngleUnit :: Radians ); const uint16_t raw = encoder . GetRawAngle (); // ANGLEUNC: without DAEC const int16_t vel = encoder . GetVelocity (); // signed 14 bit, 24.141 deg/s per LSB const float rpm = encoder . GetVelocity ( as5047u :: VelocityUnit :: Rpm ); std :: printf ( "%u (%.2f deg, %.4f rad) raw %u, vel %d (%.1f rpm) 
 " , lsb , deg , rad , raw , vel , rpm ); Value Register Range Unit GetAngle() ANGLECOM (0x3FFF) 0 to 16383 360° / 16384 = 0.022° per LSB GetRawAngle() ANGLEUNC (0x3FFE) 0 to 16383 Same, without dynamic angle error compensation GetVelocity() VEL (0x3FFC) −8192 to 8191 24.141 °/s per LSB (4.02 rpm per LSB) ANGLECOM includes the zero position and the direction. Address 0x3FFF returns ANGLEUNC instead when SetAngleOutputSource(UseANGLEUNC) is set. The datasheet specifies the velocity for −28000 rpm to 28000 rpm with a total error of ±5 %. Check the magnetic field ¶ const uint8_t agc = encoder . GetAGC (); // 0..255; 0 or 255: field out of range const uint16_t mag = encoder . GetMagnitude (); // CORDIC magnitude, kept steady by AGC const auto dia = encoder . GetDiagnostics (); // DIA (0x3FF5) std :: printf ( "AGC %u MAG %u 5V mode %u AGC low %u high %u 
 " , agc , mag , static_cast < unsigned > ( dia . bits . VDD_mode ), static_cast < unsigned > ( dia . bits . Comp_l ), static_cast < unsigned > ( dia . bits . Comp_h )); encoder . DumpStatus (); // every register, through printf Reading Healthy Problem GetAGC() Between 0 and 255, not at either end 0: field too strong (magnet too close). 255: field too weak GetMagnitude() Steady while the AGC is in range Falls when the AGC is at 255 dia.bits.LoopsFinished 1 0: the chip has not finished start-up dia.bits.MagHalf_flag 0 1: magnitude below half its target dia.bits.Comp_l , Comp_h 0 AGC at its low or high limit Configure ¶ using Hys = AS5047U_REG :: SETTINGS3 :: Hysteresis ; bool ok = true ; ok = ok && encoder . SetZeroPosition ( encoder . GetAngle ()); // here is 0 degrees ok = ok && encoder . SetDirection ( true ); // clockwise (from the top) counts up ok = ok && encoder . SetDynamicAngleCompensation ( true ); // DAEC on (default) ok = ok && encoder . SetFilterPreset ( FilterPreset :: Balanced ); // K = 2..3 ok = ok && encoder . SetHysteresis ( Hys :: LSB_1 ); ok = ok && encoder . Set150CTemperatureMode ( false ); // 3.3 V: low noise, up to 125 C return ok ; // false: a write did not read back as written These settings live in volatile registers until you burn them ( OTP programming ). Configuration lists every setting with its register and default, and two complete setups. Set up the outputs ¶ bool ok = true ; ok = ok && encoder . ConfigureInterface ( true , false , false ); // ABI on, UVW off, no PWM ok = ok && encoder . SetABIResolution ( 12 ); // 4096 steps, 1024 pulses per turn ok = ok && encoder . SetIndexPulseLength ( 3 ); // index pulse 3 LSB wide (or 1) ok = ok && encoder . SetUVWPolePairs ( 4 ); // UVW for a 4 pole-pair motor return ok ; SetABIResolution() takes 10 to 14 bits (clamped) and writes the binary ABIRES code; SetUVWPolePairs() takes 1 to 7 (clamped). For decimal pulse counts, use the register directly (next section). Use any register directly ¶ auto s2 = encoder . ReadReg < AS5047U_REG :: SETTINGS2 > (); // fields in .bits s2 . bits . ABI_DEC = 1 ; // decimal ABI counts (1000, 500, ... pulses) s2 . bits . IWIDTH = 1 ; // 1 LSB index pulse if ( ! encoder . WriteReg ( s2 , 2 )) { // verified, 2 retries return false ; } using Res = AS5047U_REG :: SETTINGS3 :: ABIResolution ; auto s3 = encoder . ReadReg < AS5047U_REG :: SETTINGS3 > (); s3 . bits . ABIRES = static_cast < uint8_t > ( Res :: Code0 ); // with ABI_DEC: 1000 pulses return encoder . WriteReg ( s3 ); Each struct in AS5047U_REG has ADDRESS , a 16-bit value and named bits . ReadReg<T>() reads it (and ERRFL); WriteReg(reg, retries) writes value and checks the read-back. The datasheet's register tables are in its "Volatile Registers" and "Non-Volatile Registers (OTP)" sections. Handle errors ¶ The chip reports errors in ERRFL (0x0001), which clears when it is read (datasheet Figure 33). Every register read inside the driver reads ERRFL after the register and ORs its bits into a set of sticky flags ; so does GetErrorFlags() and ReadReg<AS5047U_REG::ERRFL>() , so no ERRFL value the driver reads is lost. GetStickyErrorFlags() returns the flags and leaves them set; ClearStickyErrorFlags() clears them and returns what it cleared, in one atomic step. ( void ) encoder . ClearStickyErrorFlags (); // start a clean window const uint16_t angle = encoder . GetAngle ( 2 ); // then ERRFL; 2 retries on CRC const auto flags = static_cast < uint16_t > ( encoder . GetStickyErrorFlags ()); // kept until cleared if ( flags != 0U ) { if ( flags & static_cast < uint16_t > ( AS5047U_Error :: CrcError )) { std :: printf ( "CRC error: check wiring, SPI mode 1, clock 
 " ); } if ( flags & ( static_cast < uint16_t > ( AS5047U_Error :: AgcWarning ) | static_cast < uint16_t > ( AS5047U_Error :: MagHalf ))) { std :: printf ( "magnet out of range 
 " ); } return false ; // do not use this sample } std :: printf ( "angle %u 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( angle )); return true ; The getters decide on a retry from the ERRFL of their own read, so they never consume the sticky flags: the flags of every sample stay visible until you clear them. GetErrorFlags() returns the chip's ERRFL, which only shows what happened since the driver's previous read of it; the sticky flags hold everything since your last clear. Bits 0 to 10 are the ERRFL bits. Bits 11 and 12 are errors the driver detects itself; bits 13 and 14 are the warning and error bits of the chip's replies (bit 15, 14 of a 16-bit frame; datasheet Figures 22, 25 and 28). Flag ( AS5047U_Error ) Bit Meaning What to do AgcWarning 0 AGC at 0 or 255 Check the magnet distance; read DIA for which end MagHalf 1 AGC at 255 and the magnitude below half its target Magnet too far or missing P2ramWarning 2 ECC corrected one bit of the OTP settings Note it; the value is still right P2ramError 3 ECC found an uncorrectable OTP error Settings are not reliable FramingError 4 The chip could not frame the SPI transfer (for example a wrong number of clocks) Check CSn per frame and the port's len CommandError 5 Invalid command Check frame format and wiring CrcError 6 CRC of a MOSI frame was wrong Check SPI mode 1, clock, signal integrity WatchdogError 7 Internal oscillator or watchdog fault Power-cycle; replace the part if it persists OffCompError 9 Offset compensation not finished Normal right after power-on; wait 10 ms CordicOverflow 10 CORDIC overflow The angle is not valid; check the field BusError (driver) 11 The port's transfer() returned false Check the SPI driver and the bus; see Porting ReplyCrcError (driver) 12 The CRC of a 24- or 32-bit reply was wrong: MISO was corrupted Same as CrcError ; the read was rejected ReplyWarning (reply) 13 Warning bit set in a reply Look at ERRFL bits 0 to 2 in the same flags ReplyError (reply) 14 Error bit set in a reply Look at the ERRFL error bits in the same flags After any flag the datasheet asks for a read of DIA ( GetDiagnostics() ) for the details. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes. Version ¶ const char * v = as5047u :: AS5047U < MySpi >:: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0"

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one AS5047U object. Its methods read and write the chip's typed registers (listed from inc/as5047u_registers.hpp), build 16-, 24- or 32-bit frames with CRC, check writes by reading them back and collect the ERRFL error flags. The SPI interface (SpiInterface in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base with one method. The platform port is the only code you write: a class whose transfer() moves one frame over SPI with chip select held low and returns false on a bus error. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/as5047u_registers.hpp register structs ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it Core : AS5047U<SpiType> , typed registers inc/as5047u.hpp and the headers beside it Never, for a new board SPI interface : SpiInterface<> as5047u_spi_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your class Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) The core depends only on the port's transfer() . Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model of the chip. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. All notable changes to this driver are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning . [Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ Host unit tests ( -DHF_AS5047U_BUILD_TESTS=ON ) against a model of the AS5047U SPI slave, and a CI workflow. Changed ¶ CI builds all five ESP32 example apps ( ci_enabled in examples/esp32/app_config.yml ); only driver_integration_test was built before. configuration_example and full_features now check each setter's result and report the sticky flags of a failed one. Breaking (port contract): the SPI port's transfer() returns bool ( true = frame clocked, false = bus error) and every driver path propagates it: setters, WriteReg() and ProgramOTP() return false , a read-modify-write setter whose read fails writes nothing, and every failed frame sets the new AS5047U_Error::BusError sticky flag. A void transfer() still compiles and is treated as never failing; any other return type is rejected by static_assert . New ReadReg(reg, retries) overload returns whether the read worked. Datasheet "SPI Transaction", Figures 29 and 30: a read or write is a fixed sequence of frames, so a frame that was not clocked leaves the access incomplete. Breaking: GetStickyErrorFlags() no longer clears the flags; the new ClearStickyErrorFlags() clears them and returns what it cleared. The measurement getters no longer consume the flags to decide on a retry (they use the ERRFL of their own read), so the flags of every sample stay visible until the caller clears them. Datasheet Figure 33: ERRFL clears when read, so the driver's cache is the only copy. Code that relied on a get to clear must call ClearStickyErrorFlags() instead. Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, architecture, SPI protocol, OTP programming, API guide, porting, testing), code snippets compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ , Doxygen under /api/ , versioned with mike. The Jekyll site files and the doxygen-awesome submodule are gone. Fixed ¶ cmake --install now installs as5047u.ipp , which as5047u.hpp includes, so an installed copy compiles; the header includes it through the include path ( src/ is a build include directory) instead of ../src/ . The installed target is exported as hf::as5047u , the name the package config and the docs give (it was hf::hf_as5047u , which stays available as an alias). New ctest hf_as5047u_install_consumer builds a find_package() consumer against a fresh install. The write path no longer prints: a failed write verification used to printf a line from inside the driver. The cause is in the sticky flags, which the write path already fills from ERRFL. DumpStatus() , which exists to print, is unchanged. The non-standard M_PI is replaced by the constant as5047u::kPi , so the header builds where M_PI is not defined (MSVC without _USE_MATH_DEFINES , strict-ISO newlib); <cmath> is no longer included. ProgramOTP() follows the datasheet's step-by-step OTP procedure exactly (DS000637 page 41-42, Figure 60): it now clears the volatile registers before the guard-band test (step 15, which was skipped, so the guard-band comparison could pass on values still in the volatile registers), writes the PROG values of Figure 60 ( 0x01 , 0x08 , 0x40 , 0x04 ; it wrote 0x09 , 0x49 , 0x4D , 0x49 , which set PROGOTP again after the burn), compares DISABLE..ECC (0x0015..0x001B) instead of 0x0016..0x001A, checks the result of every step and stops at the first failure (it ignored every write result and could burn after a failed write). New optional OtpResult* argument reports the failed step, whether the burn started and the burned image; new VerifyOTP() performs the power-on check of steps 21 and 22. The CRC of each 24- and 32-bit reply the driver uses is checked: a corrupted reply fails the access (retried when retries allows; a failed read returns 0) and sets the new ReplyCrcError sticky flag, instead of being returned as data. The warning and error bits of the replies are recorded as the new ReplyWarning and ReplyError sticky flags. Datasheet "SPI Transaction" Figures 22, 25 and 28 (MISO data frames) and "CRC Checksum" with Figure 31. Every ERRFL value the driver reads reaches the sticky flags: GetErrorFlags() and ReadReg<ERRFL>() used to read ERRFL a second time for the sticky update, which returned 0 and dropped the flags (datasheet Figure 33). GetErrorFlags() no longer re-reads ERRFL until it reads 0. Every member of AS5047U<> compiles on current GCC and Clang: the template keyword is no longer used without a template argument list, and GetFilterParameters() no longer binds bit-fields to references. [1.0.0] ¶ The version set in cmake/hf_as5047u_build_settings.cmake ; not tagged yet. Added ¶ AS5047U<SpiType> driver over a CRTP SPI interface: angle, velocity, AGC, magnitude, diagnostics, 16-, 24- and 32-bit frames with CRC, zero position, direction, DAEC, adaptive filter presets, ABI / UVW / PWM outputs, hysteresis, OTP programming, typed register access. ESP-IDF component wrapper and ESP32 example applications.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every setting of the AS5047U, the call that changes it, its register and reset value, and two complete setups. All settings live in the non-volatile register block (0x0015 to 0x001B). Writes go to the volatile copy and are lost at power-off unless you burn them ( OTP programming ). A chip that was never programmed starts with every register at 0x0000 , which gives the defaults below. Every snippet here is compiled from tests/docs/configuration.cpp . Compile-time defaults ¶ Define these for the whole build (for example target_compile_definitions(my_app PRIVATE CONFIG_AS5047U_FRAME_24) , or in your sdkconfig.h ); inc/as5047u_config.hpp reads them. Define Effect Without it CONFIG_AS5047U_FRAME_24 The constructor's default format is SPI_24 SPI_16 CONFIG_AS5047U_FRAME_32 The constructor's default format is SPI_32 SPI_16 CONFIG_AS5047U_CRC_RETRIES=n Default retries argument of every call 0 The repository has no Kconfig file of its own; an ESP-IDF project that wants a menu entry defines these symbols in its own Kconfig.projbuild . Settings ¶ Setting (field) Call Reset value Zero position ( ZPOSM , ZPOSL ) SetZeroPosition() 0 Direction ( SETTINGS2.DIR ) SetDirection() Clockwise counts up DAEC ( SETTINGS2.DAECDIS ) SetDynamicAngleCompensation() On What 0x3FFF returns ( SETTINGS2.Data_select ) SetAngleOutputSource() ANGLECOM Adaptive filter ( DISABLE.FILTER_disable ) SetAdaptiveFilter() On Filter coefficients ( SETTINGS1.K_min , K_max ) SetFilterPreset() K = 2 to 6 150 °C in 3.3 V mode ( SETTINGS2.NOISESET ) Set150CTemperatureMode() Off: up to 125 °C ABI, UVW, PWM ( DISABLE , SETTINGS2 ) ConfigureInterface() PWM off ABI resolution ( SETTINGS3.ABIRES ) SetABIResolution() 1024 pulses Index pulse width ( SETTINGS2.IWIDTH ) SetIndexPulseLength() 3 LSB UVW pole pairs ( SETTINGS3.UVWPP ) SetUVWPolePairs() 1 ABI hysteresis ( SETTINGS3.HYS ) SetHysteresis() 1 LSB (0.17°) DAEC is the dynamic angle error compensation; SetFilterParameters() sets the filter codes directly. ABI and UVW are on after reset. Directions are seen from the top of the chip. The ABI decimal mode ( SETTINGS2.ABI_DEC ) has no setter; see below. Filter presets ¶ The adaptive filter picks a coefficient K between K_min and K_max depending on acceleration. Low K is less noise and more latency. FilterPreset K_min, K_max Velocity noise (Figure 17) Corner frequency LowNoise 0, 0 5.8 °/s rms 48 Hz Balanced 2, 3 8.4 to 19.8 °/s rms 194 to 387 Hz HighBandwidth 6, 6 244.9 °/s rms 3095 Hz SetFilterParameters() takes the 3-bit register codes, not K: the mapping is not linear (Figure 13: K_min code 000 is K = 2, 101 is K = 0; K_max code 000 is K = 6, 110 is K = 0). The presets write the right codes. ABI resolution ¶ SetABIResolution() Steps per turn Pulses per turn ABIRES 14 16384 4096 100 13 8192 2048 011 12 (default) 4096 1024 000 11 2048 512 001 10 1024 256 010 With ABI_DEC = 1 the same codes give decimal counts from 1000 down to 25 pulses per turn; set it with WriteReg() ( API guide ). Interface combinations ¶ ConfigureInterface(abi, uvw, pwm) : abi uvw pwm Outputs true false false A, B, I true false true A, B, I; PWM on W false true false U, V, W false true true U, V, W; PWM on I true true any A, B, I and U, V, W; UVW_ABI = 0, so PWM (if set) takes the W pin false false true PWM on W false false false ABI and UVW tristated Setups ¶ Motor commutation and speed control ¶ // BLDC commutation and speed: fast response, UVW to the gate driver, ABI to the MCU. bool ok = true ; ok = ok && encoder . SetDynamicAngleCompensation ( true ); // latency compensated ok = ok && encoder . SetFilterPreset ( FilterPreset :: HighBandwidth ); // K = 6 ok = ok && encoder . ConfigureInterface ( true , true , false ); // ABI and UVW, no PWM ok = ok && encoder . SetUVWPolePairs ( 7 ); ok = ok && encoder . SetABIResolution ( 14 ); // 4096 pulses per turn return ok ; Slow or static positioning ¶ // Static or slow positioning (under about 100 rpm): lowest noise. using Hys = AS5047U_REG :: SETTINGS3 :: Hysteresis ; bool ok = true ; ok = ok && encoder . SetDynamicAngleCompensation ( false ); // 0.016 deg rms less ok = ok && encoder . SetFilterPreset ( FilterPreset :: LowNoise ); // K = 0 ok = ok && encoder . SetHysteresis ( Hys :: LSB_2 ); ok = ok && encoder . ConfigureInterface ( false , false , false ); // SPI only, rest off return ok ; The datasheet recommends turning DAEC off under about 100 rpm: it removes 0.016° rms of noise and the latency it compensates does not matter at low speed. The chip samples MOSI on the falling edge of CLK Bit order MSB first Clock Up to 10 MHz (t clk ≥ 100 ns) Frame 16 bits (reads only, no CRC), 24 bits (CRC-8) or 32 bits (CRC-8 and a PAD byte) Chip select Active low, one frame per low period. The chip executes the frame on the rising edge of CSn Reply The data for a read arrives during the next frame Driver default 16-bit frames ( AS5047U_CFG::DEFAULT_FRAME_FORMAT ); writes always go out as 24-bit frames SPI protocol shows the bits of each frame, the CRC and the read and write sequences. Timing ¶ Figure 19. The two 350 ns limits are the ones a port can break: CSn low to the first clock edge, and CSn high between two frames. A hardware chip select usually meets them with one or two clock cycles of set-up and hold; a GPIO chip select toggled right next to the transfer may not. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10 or later, Clang 12 or later. The host CI builds with GCC and Clang on Ubuntu 24.04. No RTOS, heap or exceptions. The only output is DumpStatus() , which prints through printf when you call it. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-as5047u-driver.git external/hf-as5047u-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-as5047u-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-as5047u-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_as5047u ) # or the alias hf::as5047u hf_as5047u is an INTERFACE target: it carries the include directories (including the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. An installed copy works the same way. cmake --install puts the headers, the template implementation as5047u.ipp and the generated as5047u_version.h in one include directory and exports the package hf_as5047u : find_package ( hf_as5047u CONFIG REQUIRED ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::as5047u ) Option Default Effect HF_AS5047U_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic for targets that link the driver HF_AS5047U_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_as5047u/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_AS5047U_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_as5047u . The wrapper itself requires driver and freertos . How the build is organized ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_as5047u_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt Interface library, install and package export ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_as5047u/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into as5047u_version.h at configure time. A build that does not go through CMake must generate that header from inc/as5047u_version.h.in itself. Read the version at run time: const char * v = as5047u :: AS5047U < MySpi >:: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" Compile-time switches ¶ Define Effect CONFIG_AS5047U_FRAME_24 , CONFIG_AS5047U_FRAME_32 Default frame format of the constructor (otherwise SPI_16 ) CONFIG_AS5047U_CRC_RETRIES=n Default number of retries of every call (otherwise 0) Next ¶ Quickstart wires the sensor and reads an angle; Porting writes the SPI interface for your MCU.

docs.text: OTP programming ¶ How to make the zero position and the settings permanent: what the chip requires, what ProgramOTP() does, and what you still check yourself. The settings registers (DISABLE, ZPOSM, ZPOSL, SETTINGS1 to 3, ECC at 0x0015 to 0x001B) are volatile copies of the one-time-programmable memory. Every setter in the driver writes the volatile copy: it works at once and is lost at the next power cycle. Burning the OTP keeps it forever, and it can be done once per chip . One attempt per chip A burn cannot be repeated or undone, and the datasheet requires a part that fails verification to be scrapped. Program on the bench first and verify every setting in volatile form before you burn. Conditions ¶ Parameter Value Supply during the burn, 5 V mode 4.5 V to 5.5 V on VDD, 1 µF on VDD3V3 Supply during the burn, 3.3 V mode 3.3 V to 3.5 V (narrower than the 3.0 V to 3.6 V operating range) Current Up to 100 mA during the burn: the supply must deliver it Temperature 5 °C to 45 °C Frames 24- or 32-bit, with CRC The datasheet sequence and the driver ¶ The datasheet's step-by-step procedure (page 41-42, flowchart Figure 60) and what ProgramOTP() does at each step. The driver checks the result of every step and stops at the first that fails; OtpResult::failed_step names it. Step Datasheet ProgramOTP() 1 Power-on cycle Your job, before the call 2 Write the settings registers Your job: call the setters before ProgramOTP() 3 Place the magnet at the zero position Your job 4, 5 Read ANGLECOM, write it into ZPOSL[5:0] and ZPOSM[7:0] Done, each write verified 6 Read the settings Done, 0x0015..0x001B 7 to 9 ECC = 0x80 ( ECC_en ), read ECC_s from 0x3FD0, ECC = 0x80 | ECC_s Done, each write verified 10, 11 Read the settings back and compare with what was written Done, 0x0015..0x001B 12 PROG = 0x01 ( PROGEN ) Done, verified 13 PROG = 0x08 ( PROGOTP ): the burn starts Sent once, never retried; burn_started is set 14 Poll PROG until it reads 0x0001 Done; gives up after 15000 polls 15 Clear the volatile registers: 0x0000 into 0x0015..0x001B Done, each write verified 16, 17 PROG = 0x40 ( PROGVER , guard band), PROG = 0x04 ( OTPREF , reload from OTP) Done; the chip must accept each frame (no CRC, framing or command error) 18, 19 Read 0x0015..0x001B, compare with step 10 (guard-band test) Done; returns false on a difference 20 to 22 Power-on cycle, read back, compare Your job, after the call: VerifyOTP(result.written) The step text reads 0x0016..0x001A or 0x001B; Figure 60 reads and clears 0x0015 (DISABLE) too, which is also a non-volatile register, so the driver reads and compares all seven, 0x0015..0x001B. The PROG values are those of Figure 60. Steps 12 to 17 always use frames with CRC: ProgramOTP() switches to 24-bit frames for the duration when the driver is in SPI_16 mode and restores the format afterwards. Step 4 reads ANGLECOM, which already includes the zero position and the direction: start from a power-on cycle (ZPOSM = ZPOSL = 0) as step 1 asks, or the new zero is offset by the old one. A failure after the burn started failed_step 4 to 12 means nothing was burned ( burn_started is false): fix the cause and try again. From step 13 on the fuses may be burned. A part that fails step 19, or the power-on check in steps 20 to 22, must not be used: the datasheet does not allow reprogramming. Use it ¶ // The settings are in the volatile registers (configure() above), the magnet is // at the zero position, VDD is 4.5 to 5.5 V (5 V mode) or 3.3 to 3.5 V (3.3 V // mode), and the chip is at 5 to 45 C. as5047u :: OtpResult result {}; if ( ! encoder . ProgramOTP ( & result )) { // current angle becomes zero, then burns. Once. std :: printf ( "OTP step %u failed%s \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( result . failed_step ), result . burn_started ? ": do not use the part" : ", nothing burned" ); return false ; } // Step 20: cycle the supply, then steps 21 and 22: return encoder . VerifyOTP ( result . written ); VerifyOTP() is the power-on check of steps 21 and 22: after cycling the supply it reads 0x0015..0x001B and compares them with OtpResult::written , the image that was burned. Next: Configuration lists every setting the burn makes permanent.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class with one method: the SPI transfer. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls transfer() on a class you derive from as5047u::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the call is resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one AS5047U object. Its methods read and write the chip's typed registers (listed from inc/as5047u_registers.hpp), build 16-, 24- or 32-bit frames with CRC, check writes by reading them back and collect the ERRFL error flags. The SPI interface (SpiInterface in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base with one method. The platform port is the only code you write: a class whose transfer() moves one frame over SPI with chip select held low and returns false on a bus error. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/as5047u_registers.hpp register structs ; inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract bool transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) Pull CSn low, clock out len bytes from tx while storing len bytes into rx , release CSn. Return true when the frame went out, false on a bus error. len is 2, 3 or 4. The driver always passes both buffers The driver builds every byte of every frame, including the CRC and the PAD; your port only moves bytes. The port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public as5047u :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // One frame of 2, 3 or 4 bytes, full duplex, CSn low for the whole frame. // SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1), MSB first, up to 10 MHz. // Return false on a bus error: the driver call that sent the frame then fails. bool transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { platform_cs_low (); const bool ok = platform_spi_exchange ( tx , rx , len ); platform_cs_high (); // the chip executes the frame here; >= 350 ns high return ok ; } }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1), MSB first, up to 10 MHz. The clock idles low and the chip samples MOSI on the falling edge; modes 0, 2 and 3 do not work. One frame per call. CSn goes low before the first byte and high after the last. The chip executes the frame on the rising edge of CSn, so never merge two calls into one chip-select period, and never split one. CSn timing. At least 350 ns from CSn low to the first clock edge, and at least 350 ns of CSn high between frames ( Hardware ). Blocking. Return only when the frame is complete and rx is filled. The driver uses the reply of one call to build the next. Bus errors ¶ Return false from transfer() when your SDK reports a failure. The driver stops the access that sent the frame: the setters, WriteReg() and ProgramOTP() return false , ReadReg(reg) returns false , and every failed frame sets AS5047U_Error::BusError in the sticky flags, which is how the measurement getters (they return a value, 0 for a failed read) report it. A read-modify-write setter whose read fails writes nothing. Calls with a retries argument repeat a failed access. Return a bool , not your SDK's status code: the driver rejects any other return type at compile time, so an esp_err_t (where 0 is success) cannot be read as false . A port written for the earlier contract, with a void transfer() , still compiles; the driver treats it as never failing. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_as5047u_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF spi_master device in mode 1 with hardware chip select ( spics_io_num ), one spi_device_transmit() per frame, and optional logging of every frame. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it ( template class as5047u::AS5047U<MySpi>; ). Read DIA with GetDiagnostics() : LoopsFinished = 1 and a plausible VDD_mode prove that reads work. Read ERRFL with GetErrorFlags() twice: the second read should be 0. A persistent Framing_error or CRC_error points at the mode, CSn handling or the frame length. Write a setting and read it back: SetDirection(false) must return true , and ReadReg<AS5047U_REG::SETTINGS2>() must show DIR = 1. On a logic analyzer, the read of ANGLECOM in SPI_24 mode is 7F FF BD ( 0xBD is the CRC of 0x7FFF ), followed by the NOP 40 00 1B . Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each sensor one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several sensors on separate chip selects can share a bus only if the bus driver serializes whole frames.

docs.text: SPI protocol ¶ The three frame formats, the CRC, and the frame sequences the driver sends for a read and a write, with what each costs on the bus. The source is the datasheet's "SPI Transaction" section (Figures 20 to 31). The driver's side is rawReadRegister() and writeRegister() in src/as5047u.ipp . Frame formats ¶ Format MOSI (host to chip) MISO (chip to host) Use 16 bit [15] don't care, [14] R = 1, [13:0] address [15] warning, [14] error, [13:0] data Reads only, no CRC 24 bit [23] don't care, [22] RW, [21:8] address, [7:0] CRC [23] warning, [22] error, [21:8] data, [7:0] CRC Reads and writes 32 bit [31:24] PAD, [23] don't care, [22] RW, [21:8] address, [7:0] CRC [31] warning, [30] error, [29:16] data, [15:8] CRC, [7:0] PAD Daisy chains RW is 1 for a read and 0 for a write. The warning and error bits report a problem in the previous command frame; the details are in ERRFL. The driver records them from every reply with a valid CRC (every 16-bit reply) as the sticky flags ReplyWarning and ReplyError . They do not fail the access: the data in the reply is still the register content, and the ERRFL read that follows every access says what the problem was. Pick the format with the constructor or SetFrameFormat() : FrameFormat Bytes per frame Reads Writes SPI_16 2 16-bit frames Sent as 24-bit frames, then back to 16 bit SPI_24 3 24-bit frames 24-bit frames SPI_32 4 32-bit frames, PAD from SetPad() 32-bit frames The datasheet allows 16-bit frames for reads only, so the driver promotes every write in SPI_16 mode to a 24-bit frame. CRC ¶ Parameter Value Width 8 bit Polynomial 0x1D (x 8 + x 4 + x 3 + x 2 + 1) Initial value 0xC4 Reflection None, in or out Final XOR 0xFF Covered bits 24-bit frames and the 32-bit command frame: bits 23:8. 32-bit reply: bits 31:16. The PAD is never covered The initial value makes an all-zero frame invalid: 0x000000 would otherwise be a valid command. The driver computes it with AS5047U<>::ComputeCRC8(uint16_t) , a constexpr function; the host tests check it against an independent implementation for all 65536 inputs. A frame whose CRC is wrong is not executed and sets CRC_error in ERRFL. In the other direction the driver checks the CRC of every 24- and 32-bit reply whose content it uses (the data of a read, the ERRFL value, both replies of a write): a mismatch means the reply was corrupted on MISO, so the access fails, sets the ReplyCrcError sticky flag and is repeated when the call has retries left. A read that fails this way returns 0, never the corrupted value ( API guide ). 16-bit frames carry no CRC, so nothing protects their replies. Read ¶ The chip executes a command at the rising edge of CSn and returns the result during the next frame. One driver read is therefore four frames: the read command, a NOP that clocks the data out, then the same for ERRFL, so that every read also collects the error flags. sequenceDiagram participant D as Driver participant C as AS5047U D->>C: read ANGLECOM (0x3FFF) C-->>D: (previous reply, discarded) D->>C: read NOP (0x0000) C-->>D: ANGLECOM data D->>C: read ERRFL (0x0001) C-->>D: (NOP reply, discarded) D->>C: read NOP (0x0000) C-->>D: ERRFL, cleared on the chip by this read Note over D: ERRFL bits are ORed into the sticky flags Write ¶ A write is a command frame with RW = 0 followed by a data frame with the new 14-bit value. During the data frame the chip sends the old content; during the next frame it sends the new content. The driver sends a NOP as that next frame and compares what comes back with what it wrote. sequenceDiagram participant D as Driver participant C as AS5047U D->>C: write command, address n C-->>D: (previous reply) D->>C: data frame: new value C-->>D: old content of n D->>C: read NOP C-->>D: new content of n Note over D: equal: return true. Different: read ERRFL, retry or return false On a mismatch the driver reads ERRFL, which goes into the sticky flags, and tries again up to retries times. It prints nothing: the reason for a failed write is in GetStickyErrorFlags() . What a call costs ¶ Frames per call, from the sequences above. Times are derived for 24-bit frames at 10 MHz (2.4 µs of clock per frame, plus at least 350 ns of CSn high between frames and your port's own overhead); they are not measurements. Call Frames Clock time at 10 MHz GetAngle() , GetVelocity() , GetAGC() , ReadReg<>() 4 9.6 µs (6.4 µs with SPI_16 ) GetZeroPosition() 8 19.2 µs WriteReg() 3 7.2 µs SetDirection() , SetABIResolution() and other one-field setters 7 (read, then write) 16.8 µs ConfigureInterface() 14 33.6 µs A failed write verification adds four frames for ERRFL and repeats the write. A rejected reply (wrong CRC) ends the access at that frame; a retry starts it again. Daisy chains and the PAD byte ¶ In a 32-bit frame the PAD byte leads the MOSI frame and trails the MISO frame. The datasheet allows any number of PAD bits before the MOSI data so that the host can tell which device's reply it is reading. The driver sends one PAD byte, the value set with SetPad() , at the start of every 32-bit frame; it does not interpret the PAD on MISO.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the chip, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host unit tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the AS5047U SPI slave ( tests/mock_as5047u.hpp ): the frame length selects the format, the reply to a command arrives during the next frame, write data frames return the old and then the new content, wrong CRCs set ERRFL, and ERRFL clears when read. Every MOSI frame is logged, so tests check the exact bytes on the bus, and the model can fail a transfer, corrupt a reply on MISO or set the reply's warning and error bits on demand, to check that bus and reply errors reach the caller. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_AS5047U_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure CTest also runs hf_as5047u_install_consumer : it installs the build tree into build-host/install-test and builds a find_package(hf_as5047u) consumer ( tests/install_consumer/ ) that includes every public header and instantiates the driver, so a header missing from the install or a wrong exported target name fails the tests. File Covers tests/test_frames.cpp CRC-8 against an independent implementation for every input; the bytes of 16-, 24- and 32-bit reads; writes promoted to 24 bit; reply CRC checks and the reply warning and error bits tests/test_driver.cpp Velocity sign and scale, zero position split, ABIRES codes, outputs, direction, filter presets, write verification, sticky flags, angle output source, bus-error propagation, void legacy ports tests/test_otp.cpp ProgramOTP() against the datasheet procedure: the register writes of Figure 60, step 15, the guard-band test, failures before and after the burn, the poll timeout, the power-on check tests/mock_as5047u.hpp The chip model, including the OTP (burn, refresh, guard band, power-on cycle) tests/test_harness.hpp A dependency-free test registry and CHECK macros Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_as5047u_doc_snippets ) with the driver explicitly instantiated over the documented port, so every member of AS5047U<> is compiled. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host unit tests GCC and Clang build and run the tests and the doc snippets ESP32 examples build The apps in examples/esp32/app_config.yml with ci_enabled , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type C++ lint, C++ analysis clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck Docs Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse budget Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools and hf-espidf-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ The ESP32 examples are the hardware test suite: driver_integration_test runs the API against a connected sensor and prints a pass / fail summary over the serial monitor.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an AS5047U, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with DumpStatus() : it prints the angle, velocity, AGC, magnitude, ERRFL, every DIA bit and the settings registers in one go, and tells transport problems (all zeros, all ones) apart from magnet problems (AGC at a limit). Every register reads 0 or 0x3FFF ¶ Cause Check Fix No supply, or TEST not grounded 3.0 V to 3.6 V (3.3 V mode) or 4.5 V to 5.5 V (5 V mode) on VDD; TEST at GND Fix the supply; ground TEST MISO not connected, or floating Probe MISO during a frame: it must toggle Wire MISO; 0x3FFF everywhere means MISO stays high Wrong SPI mode Mode 1: CLK idles low, data sampled on the falling edge Set mode 1; modes 0, 2 and 3 do not work CSn held low across several frames CSn must go high after each transfer() One frame per chip-select period ( Porting ) 5 V mode with a 3.3 V MCU V IH is 0.7 × VDD = 3.5 V at 5 V Level-shift, or run the sensor in 3.3 V mode CRC or framing errors ¶ CrcError or FramingError in the sticky flags or in GetErrorFlags() (the chip saw a bad MOSI frame), or ReplyCrcError in the sticky flags (the driver saw a bad MISO frame). Cause Fix Clock too fast for the wiring Drop to 1 MHz; the limit is 10 MHz on a short, clean bus CSn set-up or high time under 350 ns Add chip-select set-up and hold cycles in your SPI driver A frame of the wrong length transfer() must clock exactly len bytes (2, 3 or 4) Noise on CLK Shorter traces, series resistor at the MCU, solid ground between MCU and sensor Pass a retries value (for example GetAngle(2) ) to repeat a read the chip flagged. Retries hide occasional errors; they do not fix a wiring problem. AGC at 0 or 255 ¶ AGC Meaning Fix 255, MagHalf set Field too weak: magnet too far, too small or not diametrically magnetized Move it closer; the field must be 35 mT to 70 mT at the die 0 Field too strong Move the magnet away Changes with angle Magnet off-center or tilted Center it on the package axis The angle is wrong or noisy ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Angle runs backwards DIR SetDirection(true) makes clockwise (seen from the top of the chip) increase Zero is in the wrong place Zero position not set, or lost at power-off SetZeroPosition() , then OTP programming to keep it Noisy at standstill Filter at high K, DAEC on SetFilterPreset(FilterPreset::LowNoise) , SetDynamicAngleCompensation(false) Lags at high speed DAEC off, or reading ANGLEUNC SetDynamicAngleCompensation(true) , SetAngleOutputSource(UseANGLECOM) The ABI count lags by a step after a reversal ABI hysteresis (1 LSB of 11 bit, 0.17°, by default) SetHysteresis(SETTINGS3::Hysteresis::NONE) Velocity is not zero at standstill ¶ The velocity is a 14-bit two's-complement value in 24.141 °/s per LSB. At standstill the datasheet gives 5.8 °/s rms noise at K = 0 and 244.9 °/s at K = 6 (Figure 17), so ±1 LSB with the magnet still is normal, and more is normal with a high filter K. Detect "stopped" with a threshold, not with zero. Settings are gone after a power cycle ¶ The settings registers are volatile until OTP is burned: this is expected. Burn them with ProgramOTP() once you are sure of them ( OTP programming ). A setter returns false ¶ The value did not read back as written, or a frame of the write failed. The driver prints nothing; clear the sticky flags, call the setter again and read them: Sticky flags after the call Cause CrcError The write frame was corrupted on the bus: see CRC errors above FramingError or CommandError Frame length or chip select BusError The port's transfer() returned false ReplyCrcError A reply was corrupted on MISO: see CRC errors above None The register or field is read-only, or the value does not stick Call the setter with a retries value to retry automatically.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one AS5047U object. Its methods read and write the chip's typed registers (listed from inc/as5047u_registers.hpp), build 16-, 24- or 32-bit frames with CRC, check writes by reading them back and collect the ERRFL error flags. The SPI interface (SpiInterface in inc/as5047u_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base with one method. The platform port is the only code you write: a class whose transfer() moves one frame over SPI with chip select held low and returns false on a bus error. Below it is the hardware.
